description: Graduate methods for analysing genomes at scale: read mapping and assembly, variant calling, single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, regulatory genomics, association studies, cancer and microbiome analysis, and multi-omics integration. Students implement core algorithms, run statistical pipelines on simulated cohorts and query large variant tables, finishing with a reproducible analysis project.
modelledOn: Durbin, Eddy, Krogh and Mitchison, Biological Sequence Analysis
Jones and Pevzner, An Introduction to Bioinformatics Algorithms
Gusfield, Algorithms on Strings, Trees and Sequences
Hastie, Tibshirani and Friedman, The Elements of Statistical Learning (selected chapters)
outcomes: Implement index-based read mapping and de Bruijn graph assembly and judge their accuracy and cost on large inputs.
Build a variant-calling and filtering workflow and benchmark it with precision and recall against a truth set.
Analyse bulk and single-cell expression data with appropriate count models, normalisation, clustering and multiple-testing control.
Design and interpret association, fine-mapping and polygenic-score analyses, including the effect of population structure and ancestry.
Analyse tumour and microbiome sequencing data using signature, driver and compositional methods.
Integrate several omics layers and deliver a reproducible, ethically sound analysis with documented workflow and data governance.

units.title: Sequencing data, read mapping and assembly
topics: Sequencing technologies: short-read, long-read and nanopore; error profiles; FASTQ and base quality
Index-based mapping: suffix arrays, the Burrows-Wheeler transform, FM-index and seed-and-extend; SAM/BAM/CRAM
De novo assembly with de Bruijn graphs and overlap-layout-consensus; repeats and graph simplification
Assembly assessment: N50, completeness and misassembly detection; long-read polishing
Pangenome graphs and reference bias

units.title: Variant calling at scale
topics: Genotype likelihoods: a Bayesian model of pileup evidence, ploidy and priors
Calling pipelines: duplicate marking, base-quality recalibration, haplotype-based calling, joint genotyping and the VCF format
Structural variants and copy-number change from read depth, split reads and discordant pairs
Filtering and benchmarking: truth sets, precision, recall and F-measure
African genomic diversity, reference bias and why callers trained on one ancestry underperform on another

units.title: Bulk and single-cell transcriptomics
topics: Quantification by pseudoalignment and expectation-maximisation; TPM and count matrices
Differential expression: negative-binomial models, dispersion shrinkage and false discovery rate
Single-cell protocols: droplets, UMIs, ambient RNA, doublets and quality control
Normalisation, feature selection, PCA, UMAP and graph-based clustering; marker genes
Trajectory inference, pseudotime and batch integration of datasets
Spatial transcriptomics: spot- and image-based methods, deconvolution and spatially variable genes

units.title: Epigenomics and regulatory elements
topics: ChIP-seq and ATAC-seq: peak calling, fragment-size analysis and signal tracks
Bisulfite sequencing, DNA methylation and differentially methylated regions
Chromosome conformation: Hi-C contact maps, topologically associating domains and loops
Motif discovery: position weight matrices, expectation-maximisation and scanning
Sequence-to-function deep models for regulatory activity
Predicting the effect of non-coding variants on enhancers and expression

units.title: Population genetics, GWAS and fine mapping
topics: Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, linkage disequilibrium and population structure by PCA
Genome-wide association: regression models, covariates, QQ plots, genomic inflation and Manhattan plots
Linear mixed models, relatedness and SNP heritability
Polygenic scores and their poor portability across ancestries
eQTL mapping and the multiple-testing burden
Fine mapping and colocalisation: credible sets and posterior inclusion probabilities

units.title: Cancer genomics and somatic variants
topics: Somatic versus germline calling from tumour-normal pairs; contamination and low allele fractions
Tumour purity, ploidy and clonal structure
Mutational signatures by non-negative matrix factorisation
Driver gene detection: recurrence, background mutation rate and dN/dS
Copy-number alterations, fusions and structural rearrangements
Clinical interpretation of variants and tumour boards; liquid biopsy

units.title: Metagenomics and microbiome profiling
topics: Amplicon sequencing: 16S ribosomal RNA, denoising to amplicon sequence variants
Shotgun taxonomic profiling by k-mers and marker genes
Metagenome assembly and binning into genomes
Functional profiling and pathway abundance
Antimicrobial resistance gene detection and surveillance, with Ghanaian hospital and wastewater examples
Diversity measures and compositional data analysis

units.title: Multi-omics integration
topics: Omics layers and study designs: matched versus unmatched samples; early, intermediate and late integration
Matrix factorisation and canonical correlation approaches for multi-omics data
Network-based integration and similarity network fusion
Pathway and set enrichment: over-representation analysis and gene set enrichment
Missing data, batch effects and validation of integrated findings

units.title: Pipelines, data management and ethics
topics: Workflow engines, containers and provenance for reproducible genomics
Genomic data in relational stores: variant tables, interval queries and indexing
Benchmarking, power analysis and honest reporting of genomic results
Ethics of genomic research in Africa: consent, data sovereignty, benefit sharing and privacy
Project presentations: end-to-end analysis of a cohort dataset

schedule.title: Sequencing technologies and read mapping
schedule.exercise: Compare short-read and nanopore error profiles, build a suffix array and Burrows-Wheeler transform of a short string, and explain how backward search finds a read.

tasks.title: Parse a FASTQ file, compute per-position mean base quality and read-length distribution, and trim a given adapter and low-quality tails
Build a suffix array and BWT for a 1 kb reference, and implement backward search to count and locate 20 query reads
Implement seed-and-extend mapping with a k-mer index and banded alignment, then measure mapping accuracy on 2000 simulated reads with errors

schedule.title: De novo assembly and assessment
schedule.exercise: Assemble a small genome by hand from overlapping reads using a de Bruijn graph, compute N50 for a set of contigs, and discuss why repeats break assembly.

tasks.title: Build a de Bruijn graph from 100 error-free reads with k = 21, walk the unitigs, and reconstruct the 5 kb source genome
Add errors to the reads, prune tips and bubbles from the graph, and compare contig counts before and after cleaning
Compute N50, L50 and total length for three assemblies of the same genome, and rank them with a short written justification

schedule.title: Genotype likelihoods and variant calling
schedule.exercise: Calculate genotype posteriors for a site with 12 reads from a binomial error model, run a calling pipeline on a trio, and compute precision and recall against a truth set.

tasks.title: Compute genotype likelihoods and posteriors for 0/0, 0/1 and 1/1 at a site with 12 reads and error rate 1 percent, and call the genotype
Call SNPs from a pileup file with a likelihood model, then compute precision, recall and F-measure against a given truth VCF
Review a case file where a variant caller trained on European samples misses variants in an African cohort, and decide on retraining and benchmark steps

schedule.title: RNA-seq quantification and differential expression
schedule.exercise: Quantify transcript abundance by EM on a toy ambiguous-read example, fit a negative-binomial model to counts, and control the false discovery rate with Benjamini-Hochberg.

tasks.title: Implement expectation-maximisation for transcript abundance with ambiguous reads on 3 isoforms and report TPM values after convergence
Simulate counts for 5000 genes with 3 replicates per group, fit a negative-binomial test, and count false positives before and after FDR control
Examine single-cell QC plots of counts, genes and mitochondrial fraction for 3000 cells and choose filtering thresholds with justification

schedule.title: Single-cell analysis pipeline
schedule.exercise: Cluster a matrix of 3000 cells, annotate clusters from marker genes, and explain what could go wrong with batch effects and pseudotime on a trajectory.

tasks.title: Normalise, pick 2000 variable genes, run PCA and graph-based clustering on a given single-cell count matrix, and plot the clusters
Integrate two batches of the same tissue, measure batch mixing before and after correction, and check that biological clusters remain separate
Deconvolve 100 spatial spots into cell types from a reference matrix by non-negative least squares and map the proportions on the slide grid

schedule.title: Regulatory genomics
schedule.exercise: Call peaks from a ChIP-seq coverage track, find the enriched motif among them, and argue how a non-coding variant could change gene expression through an enhancer.

tasks.title: Call peaks from a ChIP-seq signal and input control using a Poisson background, and report the number of peaks at 1 percent FDR
Run expectation-maximisation motif discovery on 200 peak sequences, build the position weight matrix, and scan a genome for sites with a threshold
Train a small convolutional model on one-hot sequences to predict enhancer activity, then score the effect of ten given variants

schedule.title: Population structure and association testing
schedule.exercise: Test Hardy-Weinberg for given genotype counts, run a regression for one SNP with covariates, and explain what the QQ plot and genomic inflation factor reveal.

tasks.title: Test 10 SNPs for Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium with a chi-square test and flag the ones that fail, with possible causes
Run a case-control association test for 10,000 simulated SNPs with and without PCA covariates, and draw the QQ plot and Manhattan plot for each
Fit a linear mixed model with a relatedness matrix on a simulated cohort with family structure, and estimate SNP heritability

schedule.title: Polygenic scores, eQTL and fine mapping
schedule.exercise: Build a polygenic score from summary statistics, measure how its accuracy drops in a second ancestry, and compute credible sets for a locus with a given LD matrix.

tasks.title: Compute a polygenic score from effect sizes, evaluate it in two simulated ancestry groups, and report variance explained in each
Map eQTLs for 200 genes against nearby SNPs, correct for multiple testing at gene level, and list significant gene-SNP pairs
Compute posterior inclusion probabilities and a 95 percent credible set for a locus with strong LD, and explain why it holds several variants

schedule.title: Somatic variants and tumour evolution
schedule.exercise: Call somatic variants from tumour-normal counts, estimate purity and clonality from allele fractions, and decompose a set of mutation spectra into signatures.

tasks.title: Call somatic SNVs from paired tumour-normal read counts with a likelihood-ratio test and exclude germline variants and low-depth sites
Decompose 50 tumour mutation catalogues into 3 signatures with non-negative matrix factorisation and assign each tumour's exposure to the signatures
Test genes for excess nonsynonymous mutations using a background rate, rank candidate drivers by q-value, and plot dN/dS per gene

schedule.title: Metagenomics and the microbiome
schedule.exercise: Profile a stool metagenome, compare two groups with a compositional method, and screen a hospital wastewater sample for antimicrobial resistance genes.

tasks.title: Assign 5000 reads to taxa by k-mer matching against a small reference database and report relative abundance with a confusion estimate
Compute Shannon alpha diversity and Bray-Curtis distances for 20 samples, then test group differences with PERMANOVA and plot an ordination
Investigate a resistance outbreak in a regional hospital: choose sampling, interpret resistance gene profiles and recommend infection-control actions against the rubric

schedule.title: Integrating omics layers
schedule.exercise: Match samples across RNA, methylation and protein data for a cohort, compare early and late integration, and extract latent factors from two views.

tasks.title: Align three data tables by sample identifier, handle samples missing in one layer, and report how many remain for each integration design
Run a canonical correlation analysis on RNA and methylation views, report the top 3 components and which features load most heavily
Build patient similarity networks per omics layer, fuse them, cluster the fused network, and test if clusters differ in survival

schedule.title: Enrichment, validation and robustness
schedule.exercise: Run over-representation and gene set enrichment on a ranked gene list, and design a validation and sensitivity analysis for an integrated finding.

tasks.title: Test a list of 150 genes for pathway enrichment with the hypergeometric test, correct for multiple testing, and explain the top three pathways
Mask 20 percent of entries in a multi-omics matrix, impute them, and measure how the reconstruction error changes the clustering result
Check an integrated signature on a held-out cohort with a different batch, and report how much of its performance survives and why

schedule.title: Pipelines, data management and ethics
schedule.exercise: Wrap an analysis as a documented workflow with fixed software versions, store variant calls in a relational table, and present the genomic project with its limits and ethical safeguards.

tasks.title: Load 100,000 variants into a table, add an index, and query by genomic interval to compare the plans and timings before and after indexing
Write queries that join variants, genes and sample genotypes to list rare damaging variants shared by affected family members but absent in controls
Handle a consent and data-sharing request for a genomic cohort in a case file, balancing community benefit, privacy and sovereignty against the rubric
